title: Error in Alert_on_HTTP_Response_Code_Errors.js
body:
### Describe the bug: This may be a configuration issue on my end, but I do get a script error in a script included in the `stable` image, which I can reproduce and mitigate. I wanted to run the packaged `zap-api-scan.py` but generate some different reports. My understand is that the way to go about this is to use the Automation Framework rather than the packaged scans. I've tried to reproduce the same scan that is run by the script using a plan instead. However, when I activate one of the scripts that is loaded by `zap-api-scan.py` I get an execution error. ### Steps to reproduce the behavior: OpenAPI spec ```yaml openapi: 3.1.0 info: title: Simple API description: A simple API with a single GET endpoint version: 1.0.0 servers: - url: http://localhost:8081 paths: /: get: summary: Get description: Gets nothing responses: '200': description: Success content: {} ``` Plan to reproduce the error. ```yaml env: contexts: - name: localhost urls: - http://host.docker.internal:8081 jobs: - type: passiveScan-config parameters: maxAlertsPerRule: 10 - type: script parameters: action: add engine: "ECMAScript : Graal.js" type: httpsender name: Alert_on_HTTP_Response_Code_Errors.js source: /home/zap/.ZAP_D/scripts/scripts/httpsender/Alert_on_HTTP_Response_Code_Errors.js - type: script parameters: action: enable name: Alert_on_HTTP_Response_Code_Errors.js - type: openapi parameters: apiFile: /zap/wrk/openapi.yaml context: localhost targetUrl: http://host.docker.internal:8081 - type: passiveScan-wait - type: activeScan parameters: context: localhost policy: API-Minimal - type: report parameters: template: traditional-json reportFile: /zap/wrk/af-report.json reportTitle: JSON report ``` Python script for the target server. ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 from http.server import HTTPServer, BaseHTTPRequestHandler class SimpleHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler): def do_GET(self): if self.path == '/': self.send_response(200) else: self.send_response(500) self.end_headers() def run_server(): server_address = ('', 8081) httpd = HTTPServer(server_address, SimpleHandler) httpd.serve_forever() if __name__ == '__main__': run_server() ``` Invoke ZAP like this to mimic `zap-api-scan.py`. ``` docker run --rm --net host -v $(pwd):/zap/wrk mirror.gcr.io/zaproxy/zap-stable zap.sh -cmd -autorun /zap/wrk/plan.yaml -addonupdate -addoninstall pscanrulesBeta -addoninstall ascanrulesAlpha -config stats.pkg.apiscan-api=1 ``` This eventually fails with the following error message. ``` Automation plan failures: An error occurred with the script: Alert_on_HTTP_Response_Code_Errors.js. Error: TypeError: invokeMember (setEvidence) on org.parosproxy.paros.core.scanner.Alert failed due to: Cannot convert '[object Array]'(language: JavaScript, type: Array) to Java type 'java.lang.String': Invalid or lossy primitive coercion. ``` The problem seems to be [here](https://github.com/zaproxy/zaproxy/blob/main/docker/scripts/scripts/httpsender/Alert_on_HTTP_Response_Code_Errors.js#L81). I think the regexp match is returning an array, but `setEvidence` expects a string. If I modify this line to `alert.setEvidence(msg.getResponseHeader().toString().match(regex)[0])` the plan passes, and I get output from it in the alerts in the JSON report. ```json ... { "pluginid": "100000", "alertRef": "100000", "alert": "A Server Error response code was returned by the server", "name": "A Server Error response code was returned by the server", "riskcode": "1", "confidence": "3", "riskdesc": "Low (High)", "desc": "

A response code of 500 was returned by the server.

This may indicate that the application is failing to handle unexpected input correctly.

Raised by the 'Alert on HTTP Response Code Error' script

", ... ``` ### Expected behavior: I expected the plan to pass and a report to be generated. What I can't figure out is why I don't see this problem when running `zap-api-scan.py`. ### Software Versions: zaproxy/zap-stable ### Screenshots: _No response_ ### Errors from the zap.log file: _No response_ ### Additional context: _No response_ ### Would you like to help fix this issue? - [ ] Yes
